I was a headhunter for  aerospace and defense engineers in the late 1980's. We had to prepare candidates for interviews and this would have been excellent advice. 
And then there's the guy who seems such a perfect fit...and he shows up late, wearing purple socks, and chewing gum 🎱

I hate that this makes sense and works. It's ALL just so corporate, LinkedIn coded it hurts.

Framing your identity around being useful to another person or entity, even if it's for the purpose of getting the bag - BECAUSE it is the reason of getting the bag - makes me sick.

Fact is that in an interview you are at the mercy of the person or group you have in front of you and their own style, which is unknown to you. And each mind is a world.

One of them will like straight forward answers, the other one will like to know your story, another one will love data talk, another will analyze your analysis/synthesis capabilities.

You can summarize who you are in 20 words and the person in front will think of you that you are concise, laser focus or simply that you didn’t put the minimum effort in that answer depending on who he is and what he/she/they expect(s) from you. You will never please everyone.

Something extremely useful, is before answering, requesting the context of what the group wants to hear to level up the communication channel.

Wouldn't you like to work with people who, when they want to find out something about you, say "tell me about yourself," and when they want to know what you can do for their company, ask "what can you do for my company?" Maybe, for a change, we should demand transparency and honesty from recruiters, rather than traps and ambushes, waiting for every slip-up and beating around the bush so that they can catch a future employee with a tricky question.

👍 I ended up & then retired from working in a government agency as a legal secretary - probably the most defined job environment out there.  It's not about the job description, it was about my commitment to serve the needs of another person/entity.  In my case, I served the people of my state by providing clerical support to the attorneys I reported to, to ensure their best performance in service to the people of our state.  To me that's what a job in any sector, including self-employment, should be about:  How can I be of service within the scope of my skills, background and commitment to service?
